comments.text:
Watching all this for the past few years, I think that LLM isn't about commercializing AI - its about justifying multi-billion dollar inference data center builds.   What makes LLM particularly good at this is the exponential rise in physical resource consumption as you go into deeper "memory" parameters where the model tries to keep more information to better navigate the dataspace.  Run short on that memory or on resources and your LLM acts like a person in a room filled with nitrogen and very little oxygen.  Its not very often devs allow an n^n time-power scale as you dive deeper into the chug.  Nvidia must be really happy.  

First - I think if Musk could have commercialized this he would have.  LLMs are interesting but the deeper you dig the more toy-like they become.  Sure, might be good for some quick/short sanity checks and maybe getting a random look on something if you're stuck on a thought-rail somewhere, but its still the human in the pilot's seat for the initial takeoff and direction and then at the end when it comes time to land the plane, as it were.  There's not a lot of commercial value in that especially considering that the community will eventually figure out how to reduce the resource cost so that a smart phone can handle these things.  I've got a feeling that this is just an excuse to build up tons and tons of compute resources.  

Second - Open Source is GOOD.  Digging at Open models allows people to see and understand how these things actually work.  Made me always roll my eyes when people like altman got up and claimed: "OMG! THIS IS SO DANGEROUS!  WE DON'T KNOW HOW IT DOES WHAT IT DOES!  REGULATE IT!  MEANWHILE WE ARE TAKING IT TO THE NEXT LEVEL!!!  BUY OUR PRODUCT!!!"  ... Altman wants the regulation to stop people from experimenting with it and making something that isn't under his "control".  OpenAI feels like a crypto scam.  Meanwhile I can respect Musk for Open-Sourcing this.  I still think he's off the mark on a lot of things - but this?  This is probably the best decision he's made in the last decade.   

Third - The money and interest in LLMs and Diffusion has accelerated things over all.   So having large models like this in the public domain will get a lot more people interested in understanding and working in this world.   That will help develop better hardware and software paradigms that will bring actually useful AI systems online a lot faster than the pace we were on just a few years ago.  And that's going to improve our medical and material science capacities by leaps and bounds. I think that instead of being 30-40 years away from our first true sentient/sapient AI systems... we might be less than a decade away now - especially if enough people focus on the hardware andd software involved.  LLMs are advanced toys.   It won't take long for us to get serious about making real tools from these techniques.  And Open Source models will help us do that.
